answer: A peer-to-peer attestation layer forces nodes to broadcast periodic state proofs across an unpredictable routing topology. Like a zephyr shifting through a valley, these signals must traverse random paths to reach validators. If a cluster of identities secretly shares a backend, their simultaneous broadcasts create a localized network gale, instantly exposing the shared server. Furthermore, validators drop random whisper queries requiring immediate responses; clones relying on one central orchestrator will inevitably fail these whispers, triggering a cluster-wide slash.
